adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:50 — `TopicView.expects(:new)` has no `.returns`, leaving `@topic_view` nil; the example passes only because views aren't rendered.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when a `topic_id` is found it assigns `@topic_view = TopicView.new(...)`. In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, the example sets `TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})` but does not provide a return value. With Mocha, an `expects` without `.returns(...)` returns `nil`, so `@topic_view` becomes `nil` during the request. The spec still passes because controller specs don’t render views by default (no `render_views`), so the template code that would dereference `@topic_view` isn’t exercised. This is a real, verifiable flaw in the test (it can mask issues / becomes brittle if views are rendered).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — `open(url).read` with no `require 'open-uri'` in this file (only poll_feed.rb:7 has it; verified by grep). Reached from topic_retriever.rb:52 and disqus.thor, where `Kernel#open` treats the URL as a filename → Errno::ENOENT.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — `i.content.scrub` NoMethodErrors on nil for RSS 2.0 feeds (simple-rss stores `<description>`/`content_encoded`, not `content`), aborting the entire item loop.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33 — `i.id` is nil for RSS 2.0 (`<guid>`), so a nil url reaches `import` and the item is silently dropped.

adjudication.rationale:
In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the URL selection logic is:

```ruby
url = i.link
url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//
```

If `i.link` is missing/blank (or non-http) and `i.id` is nil/blank (which is plausible for RSS 2.0 items where the identifier is typically exposed as `guid`, not `id`), then `url` becomes nil/blank. `TopicEmbed.import` immediately returns unless `url =~ /^https?:\/\//`, so such items are silently skipped. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 + app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 — CRITICAL stored XSS: raw_html cook method returns `raw` verbatim as `cooked` (skipping post_analyzer.cook, Discourse's only sanitizer) and the view emits `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces a new `cook_method` enum with `:raw_html` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw` when that mode is set, explicitly skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook`). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` using content fetched from external RSS/HTTP sources, and the added spec asserts `post.cooked.should == post.raw`, confirming the intent to persist/serve unsanitized HTML. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — CRITICAL: `url` interpolated unescaped into `<a href='#{url}'>` AFTER Readability sanitization; `absolutize_urls`/Nokogiri does not strip it. Verified payload yields `<a href="..." onmouseover="alert(1)">`. Reachable unauthenticated via `GET /embed/best?embed_url=...` with a forged Referer.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35-36 — HIGH: RSS path applies no tag/attribute whitelist at all (unlike import_remote), and `CGI.unescapeHTML` actively re-decodes a well-behaved feed's escaped `<script>` into an executable tag.

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` the feed item body is taken as `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and passed into `TopicEmbed.import`. That path creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged for `raw_html`, skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The embed view renders `raw post.cooked`, so any HTML in the feed content is rendered directly. `CGI.unescapeHTML` will turn escaped tags like `<script>` into actual `<script>` tags, making script execution possible. By contrast, `import_remote` uses `ruby-readability` with explicit tag/attribute allowlists, but `poll_feed` does not apply any whitelist/sanitization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — HIGH SSRF: `invalid_host?` validates only the initial hostname; open-uri then follows up to 64 redirects with no re-validation and no RFC1918/loopback blocking, and the body is imported into a rendered post (exfiltrating SSRF). `.read` has no size cap → worker OOM.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` only compares `URI(@embed_url).host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, but `TopicEmbed.import_remote` then does `open(url).read` (open-uri). open-uri will automatically follow HTTP redirects (up to a limit) and there is no re-validation of the redirected-to host/IP, nor any blocking of loopback/RFC1918 ranges, so a URL on the allowed host could redirect to internal metadata/localhost targets (SSRF). Additionally, `.read` pulls the entire response into memory with no size cap, making the Sidekiq job vulnerable to large-response memory exhaustion (OOM).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 — `invalid_host?` constrains `.host` only, not scheme; `ftp://<embeddable_host>/…` reaches open-uri's FTP handler. The `/^https?/` guard (topic_embed.rb:11) runs only after the fetch.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` only compares `URI(@embed_url).host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and does not restrict the URI scheme. Therefore an `embed_url` like `ftp://<embeddable_host>/...` will pass `invalid_host?` (same host) and reach `fetch_http`, which calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which does `open(url).read` (open-uri supports FTP). The `/^https?/` check exists only in `TopicEmbed.import`, but that runs *after* the `open(url).read` fetch has already occurred, so it doesn’t prevent non-HTTP(S) fetching.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:49-50 — MEDIUM: ruby-readability 0.5.7 filters attribute *names* only (verified in gem source), so `<a href="javascript:...">` survives the whitelist, survives absolutize_urls, and is emitted by `raw post.cooked`.

adjudication.rationale: Yes: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` passes `doc.content` (HTML) from `ruby-readability` straight into `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In `Post#cook`, `:raw_html` returns `raw` and bypasses Discourse’s normal cooking/sanitization pipeline, and `embed/best.html.erb` renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. The only additional processing (`absolutize_urls`) rewrites only relative URLs starting with `/` and does not validate/sanitize `href`/`src` values or block dangerous schemes like `javascript:`. Therefore, if the fetched page/feed contains `<a href="javascript:...">` (or similar), it can be persisted and emitted as-is in the embed iframe, which is a real XSS risk introduced by this diff. The finding’s core issue is present even without relying on the gem-source claim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — HIGH unauthenticated amplification: `embed_url` goes from `params.require` straight to `Jobs.enqueue` with no host check and no rate limit; the only throttle lives inside the job, is keyed on the full URL (`?nonce=N` bypasses it), and is disabled entirely by `no_throttle`.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26,28 — MEDIUM: `X-Frame-Options = "ALLOWALL"` is not a valid token, so the route ships with no framing control; the only compensating gate is `Referer`, which any non-browser client sets freely.
matched_golden_ids: The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that setting `X-Frame-Options` to `ALLOWALL` results in ineffective/no framing protection and notes the only gate is `Referer`, which can be freely spoofed—matching the golden’s core clickjacking/Referer-bypass concern. It does not mention the specific nil-referer empty-string fallback masking failures, but the primary underlying issue is the same.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — MEDIUM: new `skip_validations` opt bypasses `Validators::PostValidator` (post.rb:40) on edit — post-length, unique-post and spam/host validations — alongside `bypass_rate_limiter: true`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `PostRevisor#update_post` from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, which explicitly allows callers to bypass all ActiveRecord validations (including any `Validators::PostValidator` hooked into `Post`). The new code path is exercised in this diff: `TopicEmbed.import` updates an existing embedded post via `revisor.revise!(user, ..., skip_validations: true, bypass_rate_limiter: true)`, meaning edited/imported content can be persisted without length/uniqueness/spam/host/etc validation checks. This is a concrete behavior change introduced by the patch, not speculative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — LOW: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is substring containment, not origin equality; a prefix-substring origin passes. No `e.source` check.
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core issue: using `indexOf` for origin validation performs substring checks rather than strict origin equality, allowing malicious lookalike domains (e.g., `evil-discourseUrl.com`) to bypass the check. Extra note about missing `e.source` check doesn’t change the underlying match.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9 — LOW: no type coercion on `params.require(:embed_url)`; `embed_url[]=a&embed_url[]=b` yields an Array, `URI()` raises ArgumentError which the `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` does not catch → unrescued job death and retry-queue flooding.

adjudication.rationale: `EmbedController#best` assigns `embed_url = params.require(:embed_url)` with no coercion/validation. In Rails, a query like `embed_url[]=a&embed_url[]=b` makes `params[:embed_url]` an `Array`, and `require` will return that array. When there’s no existing embed, the controller enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` with `embed_url` set to that array. `RetrieveTopic` passes it into `TopicRetriever`, whose `invalid_host?` does `URI(@embed_url).host` and only rescues `URI::InvalidURIError`. Passing an `Array` to `URI()` raises a non-`InvalidURIError` (e.g., `TypeError`/`ArgumentError`), so the job will error and (with default Sidekiq retries) can cause repeated retries/failure spam. This failure path is verifiable from the diff; the only minor mismatch is that the `rescue` mentioned is in `TopicRetriever`, not `EmbedController` itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — LOW: `t[:link]` reaches `Kernel#open` with no validation; a `|`-prefixed string in a vendor XML export executes as a shell command on Ruby < 3.0.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` to call `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`. In `app/models/topic_embed.rb`, `import_remote` does `open(url).read` with no validation/sanitization before calling `TopicEmbed.import`. Although `TopicEmbed.import` later regex-checks the URL, that happens after `open(url)` has already been executed. Since `open` here is `Kernel#open`, a `url` value beginning with `|` can invoke `IO.popen` and execute a shell command, so an attacker-controlled `t[:link]` from the Disqus XML could lead to command execution when running the importer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — attacker-controlled `request.referer` interpolated into a single-quoted JS string. NOT exploitable as written (Rails escapes `'`→`'`, `<`→`<`, and entities aren't decoded in raw-text script content), but `&`→`&` corrupts referers with query strings so postMessage throws SyntaxError; the safety is incidental, not intentional.
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same underlying pattern: attacker-controlled `request.referer` is interpolated into a JavaScript string in the view without context-appropriate escaping. The candidate disputes exploitability due to Rails’ HTML escaping behavior, but it still identifies the same potential XSS class issue (untrusted header in JS context) that the golden comment expects.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85 + app/models/topic_embed.rb:37 — `save`'s return value is discarded and `revise!` returns true unconditionally, yet the caller then advances `content_sha1` via `update_column`. A failed save leaves stale content marked as current, so every later poll sees "unchanged" — permanently frozen, silently.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:32 — `Post` includes Trashable (default_scope deleted_at: nil), so a soft-deleted post makes `embed.post` nil → `PostRevisor.new(nil)` NoMethodErrors at post_revisor.rb:27, killing the poll for every subsequent item.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` when the content hash changes. A `belongs_to :post` association can return `nil` if the referenced post is not visible/available (e.g., deleted/soft-deleted under a default scope, or the row is missing since there are no FK constraints shown). In that case `PostRevisor` will later call methods on `@post` (e.g., `@post.acting_user = ...`), producing a `NoMethodError` and aborting the feed/job loop. The diff introduces no guard for this case, so the failure mode is real; the specific “Trashable default_scope” rationale isn’t shown in the diff, but the nil-dereference risk is present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:32-38 — `belongs_to :topic/:post` with NOT NULL columns but no FK, no `dependent:`, no cleanup. Combined with UNIQUE(embed_url), deleting an embedded topic bricks that article URL forever: topic_id_for_embed returns a dangling id and perform_retrieve bails because the row still exists, so it can never self-heal.

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. The diff introduces `TopicEmbed` records with `topic_id`/`post_id` NOT NULL and a UNIQUE index on `embed_url`, but provides no FK constraints or `dependent:` cleanup on `belongs_to :topic` / `:post` (migration `create_topic_embeds` only adds a unique index). If the associated topic/post is deleted, the `topic_embeds` row can remain. Then:
- `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` will still return the deleted topic_id (it just `pluck`s), and `EmbedController#best` will try `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)`, likely failing or behaving incorrectly for a missing topic.
- `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` will bail out early on `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`, preventing re-import/self-healing.
- `TopicEmbed.import` will find the stale embed, set `post = embed.post` (nil), and on update path would crash at `PostRevisor.new(post)`.
This “dangling TopicEmbed bricks the URL” failure mode is directly verifiable from the added code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 — `t.string :embed_url` is varchar(255); feed/article URLs routinely exceed that → PG::StringDataRightTruncation mid-import. Should be `:text`. (The btree index-size concern specifically does not hold — 255 is far under the limit.)

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `topic_embeds.embed_url` as `t.string`, which in Rails maps to a `varchar(255)` (no `limit` specified). The code stores arbitrary remote URLs into this column (`TopicEmbed.create!(embed_url: url)` from RSS and `import_remote`), with no length validation or truncation. If an imported URL exceeds 255 characters (common with querystrings/UTM params), Postgres will raise a `StringDataRightTruncation` / value-too-long error and the import/job will fail. This is a concrete correctness issue introduced by the schema in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15,79 — `embed_url` is the identity key with zero canonicalization, so `/a`, `/a/`, `/a?utm_source=rss` and case-differing hosts are distinct rows → duplicate topics for one page. This is the core of what the task title promises and it is not implemented.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the lookup key is the raw `url` string: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`, and the unique index added in the migration is also on the raw `:embed_url` column (`add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`). There is no normalization/canonicalization step (no URI parsing/rebuilding, no stripping query params/fragments, no host downcasing, no trailing-slash normalization). `topic_id_for_embed` likewise does an exact match on `embed_url`. Therefore, URLs that represent the same page but differ in superficial ways (trailing slash, tracking query params, host case, etc.) will be treated as distinct and can create duplicate topics/rows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:4-5 — no index on `topic_id` or `post_id`; the topic→embed direction is a sequential scan.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` creates `topic_id` and `post_id` columns but only adds an index on `embed_url` (`add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`). There is no index on `topic_id` or `post_id`, so any lookups filtering by those columns (e.g., `TopicEmbed.where(topic_id: post.topic_id)` as used in the added spec, and any future/topic-centric queries) will require a sequential scan of `topic_embeds` as it grows. This is a verifiable schema/performance defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — `default: 1` is a bare literal duplicating `Post.cook_methods[:regular]` with nothing linking them; a new first enum member silently reinterprets every existing row.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `Post.cook_methods` is defined as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` and the migration sets `cook_method` default to `1`. In this codebase `Enum` appears to be 1-based (e.g., `Post.types` uses `Enum.new(:regular, ...)` and Discourse historically stores `:regular` as `1`), so `default: 1` is consistent with `:regular` and not a verifiable bug here. The concern about “a new first enum member reinterpreting existing rows” is a general hypothetical risk of integer-backed enums and isn’t demonstrated as a defect introduced by this diff (and would remain even if the migration referenced `Post.cook_methods[:regular]` at migration time).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27-28 — `setnx` then `expire` is non-atomic; a worker death between the two leaves the key permanently unexpired, throttling that URL forever with no recovery path.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle key is created with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only then given a TTL via a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These two operations are not atomic. If the worker/process dies or raises between `setnx` succeeding and `expire` executing, the key will exist without an expiration. On subsequent calls, `setnx` will return false and the method will treat it as "retrieved recently" forever (no code path deletes or re-expires the key), permanently throttling that embed_url.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:79 — `pluck(:topic_id).first` materializes the full array with no LIMIT.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed`, `where(embed_url: embed_url).pluck(:topic_id).first` does call `pluck` (which returns an array) and then takes the first element in Ruby, but in this diff `topic_embeds.embed_url` is backed by a **unique index** (`add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`). That guarantees the query can return at most one row, so there is no “full array” to materialize beyond a single element. This is at most a micro-optimization/style suggestion (adding `limit(1)`), not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — `contents << "…"` mutates the caller's String in place; a reused/memoized string double-appends the footer and produces a spurious sha1 change (and raises on a frozen string).

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the line `contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends to the passed-in `contents` String in place. That is a concrete side effect visible in the diff: if the caller reuses the same String object across calls (e.g., memoized/held reference), the footer will be appended multiple times and the computed `content_sha1 = Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)` will change even when the original content didn’t. Additionally, `<<` will raise if a frozen String is passed. These behaviors follow directly from Ruby String semantics and the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64,70 — `absolutize_urls` corrupts protocol-relative URLs: `//cdn.example.com/x` becomes `http://host/cdn.example.com/x` (verified with Nokogiri). Extremely common in feeds.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, both link and img rewriting logic treat any value that `start_with?('/')` as a site-relative path. Protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x` also start with `/`, so they enter this branch; `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both leading slashes, producing `cdn.example.com/x`, and the code prefixes it with the article host (`prefix`), yielding `http://<article-host>/cdn.example.com/x`, which is incorrect. This is a concrete correctness bug introduced by the current implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:56-76 — relative-without-slash (`images/x.jpg`) left broken; `srcset`, `<iframe src>`, `<video src>`, `<source src>`, `<base href>` never rewritten. Only `a[href]`/`img[src]` handled.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, the code only rewrites URLs for `a[href]` and `img[src]` when the attribute value starts with `/` (root-relative). It does not rewrite other common relative forms like `images/x.jpg` or `../img.png`, and it ignores other URL-bearing attributes/tags (`srcset`, `iframe[src]`, `video/source[src]`, etc.). Since `import`/`poll_feed` rely on `absolutize_urls` to “convert any relative URLs to absolute,” embedded/imported HTML containing these forms will remain relative and can break when rendered in Discourse. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` runs a scheduled job inline inside a per-request job: every embed cache-miss triggers a full-feed fetch + N post creates synchronously. `sidekiq_options retry: false` does not apply to a direct `.new.execute`, so RetrieveTopic retries the entire feed import on every failure.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb, perform_retrieve calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` directly when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. This runs the feed polling logic inline (including `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterating `rss.items.each` to call `TopicEmbed.import`), rather than enqueueing it as a Sidekiq job. Because it’s invoked via `.new.execute` and not through Sidekiq, `Jobs::PollFeed`’s `sidekiq_options retry: false` won’t govern retries/behavior; failures in this inline call will bubble up to the caller (e.g., the `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` job), which typically can be retried by Sidekiq, causing the full feed poll/import to be re-run on retry. This is a concrete behavior visible in the diff and can lead to repeated full-feed fetches and imports on embed cache misses/failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb (whole file) — model performs outbound HTTP, readability extraction, DOM rewriting, and post creation/revision with no service boundary; consequently `import_remote` has zero test coverage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `TopicEmbed.import_remote` which performs outbound HTTP (`open(url).read`) and readability parsing inside the ActiveRecord model, but that is an architectural/maintainability critique rather than a clear bug/security/correctness defect that can be verified from the diff alone. The specific sub-claim that `import_remote` has no direct test coverage is verifiable: `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` exercises `.import` but never calls `.import_remote`. Overall, the finding is mostly a vague design concern, not a concrete defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 vs lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 — two divergent ad-hoc host validators (referer host vs embed_url host), each with its own rescue, neither normalizing case/port/`www.`; a fix to one won't reach the other.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce two separate host checks: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` compares `URI(request.referer).host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, while `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` compares `URI(@embed_url).host` to the same setting. However, these are validating *different* things (the embedding page’s origin vs. the URL being retrieved) and both are consistently tied to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. The proposed issue is primarily about duplication/normalization/maintainability (case/port/www), and the diff does not show a concrete bug or security flaw resulting from this divergence; strict equality may be intentional. Therefore it’s not a clearly verifiable defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:25 and lib/topic_retriever.rb:49 — byte-identical user lookup duplicated, and TopicRetriever omits PollFeed's `embed_by_username.present?` guard, so the two paths already disagree on preconditions.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Jobs::PollFeed#execute`, the job only runs when `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.present?`, but `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` unconditionally does `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase`. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:130-133 — the early return bypasses `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, …)` for exactly the least-trusted content and also discards the caller's `*args`/cooking_options; a cross-cutting plugin-contract change smuggled into an embedding feature.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29-37 — no rescue around `open`/`SimpleRSS.parse` and no per-item error isolation; with `retry: false` one 404/malformed item loses the entire hourly run with no operator-visible state.

Network errors (timeouts, DNS, 404), invalid/malformed feed data, or parsing errors will raise and abort the job. Additionally, the loop processes each `rss.items` entry without per-item isolation; e.g., `i.content.scrub` will raise if `content` is nil/non-string, causing the entire run to stop on a single bad item. Since the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, a failure will not be retried and will effectively drop that hourly poll attempt unless manually noticed/handled elsewhere. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:14,16 — `post.url` and `post.user` called per post with no eager-load contract specified at the `TopicView.new` call site (N+1 risk; TopicView is outside the snapshot so preloading is unconfirmed — which is itself the coupling problem).

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/site_settings.yml:354 — `embeddable_host` as a single scalar bakes "exactly one host" into the setting's shape; a second host requires a setting-type migration plus rewrites of both validators.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — `force: true` added to an ALREADY-SHIPPED migration for an unrelated table; compiles to DROP TABLE IF EXISTS, is a no-op for existing installs, and silently destroys top_topics on any schema rebuild.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration (`20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`) from `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` drops the table if it already exists before creating it, which is a destructive behavior. Because this is an already-shipped migration, altering it retroactively is risky: while it won’t run on typical existing installs that have already recorded the migration as applied, if this migration is ever re-run against a DB where `top_topics` exists (e.g., partial rebuilds, manual migration replays, or environments with the table but missing migration state), it would silently drop the table and data. The finding’s “no-op for existing installs” part is accurate; the “any schema rebuild” phrasing is a bit broad, but the core data-loss risk is real and verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — `force: true` on a brand-new table can never be needed; converts "table already exists" into silent data loss. Inconsistent with the sibling new migration, which correctly omits it.

For a normal forward-only migration, this is not necessary and is risky, so the finding points to a real potential correctness/data-loss issue present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:116 — the `-c/--category` CLI flag and its Category lookup are deleted; `disqus import -c Blog` now fails with "Unknown switches" and no deprecation path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` dropped, so imported OPs are stamped today while their replies (line 162) keep original dates; the parsed created_at at line 60 is now dead data.

TopicEmbed.import_remote/import ultimately calls PostCreator without passing any created_at option, so the created post will default to “now” instead of the thread’s original timestamp. adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — converts an offline XML import into one live HTTP fetch per thread with no rescue; a single dead permalink aborts the whole import.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the import path was changed from creating a topic/post directly from the Disqus XML data to calling `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` (open-uri) with no rescue/handling. Any network failure, timeout, non-200 response, or invalid URL will raise an exception and abort the Thor task, whereas previously it did not depend on a live HTTP fetch per thread. This is a concrete robustness/correctness regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:149 — `if post.present?` now silently swallows whole threads whose link isn't http(s), where the old path always created the topic.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the import path changed from always attempting `PostCreator.new(... raw: "[[Permalink](#{t[:link]})]")` to `post = TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` and then only processing the thread when `post.present?`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` ultimately calls `TopicEmbed.import`, which immediately returns `nil` unless `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`. So any Disqus thread whose `t[:link]` is missing or not http(s) will now yield `post == nil` and the thread will be skipped with no message, whereas the old code did not enforce an http(s) scheme and would still create a topic (subject to other validations).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:13 — pure blank-line deletion in a core class, unrelated to embedding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_creator.rb:216 — duplicates the pass-through idiom of the whitelist loop three lines above; adding `:cook_method` to that array was the in-idiom change. No live bug (Enum is 1-based, `1.present?` is true).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Gemfile:210-211 — both gems added but only Gemfile_rails4.lock regenerated; the Gemfile's own dual-boot shim (lines 3-41) falls back to the untouched `Gemfile.lock` under RAILS3=1, so that boot fails `bundle check`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20-22 — `feed_key` memoizes a "feed-modified:<sha1>" redis key and is called from nowhere (grep-confirmed). Dead scaffolding for a conditional-GET that was never wired; every poll re-downloads the whole feed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1 — `require_dependency 'email/sender'` with no Email reference in the file; copy-paste residue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:1 — `require_dependency 'nokogiri'` misapplies the Rails autoloader to a gem that Bundler already required (Gemfile:111, no `require: false`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:33 — comment "Update the topic if it changed" is false: only the post body is revised; PostRevisor has no title/topic path, so a changed feed title never propagates.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing embed is found (`else` branch), the code only revises the post body via `PostRevisor.new(post).revise!(user, absolutize_urls(url, contents), ...)` and updates `content_sha1`. The `title` argument is never applied to the existing topic/post, and `content_sha1` is computed only from `contents`, so a feed title change (even without content change) will never propagate. Thus the comment "Update the topic if it changed" is misleading/incorrect, and the diff introduces a real correctness gap for title updates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:2 — header comment "Creates and Updates Topics" claims topic updates that never happen.

adjudication.rationale: The comment in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` says it "Creates and Updates Topics" from a feed. The job calls `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)`, and `TopicEmbed.import` explicitly handles both cases: (1) when no existing `TopicEmbed` exists, it creates a new topic/post; (2) when an embed already exists and the SHA changes, it revises the existing post via `PostRevisor` and updates `content_sha1`. That is a concrete “update” behavior (updating the embedded topic’s post content), so the comment is not demonstrably false based on the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:25 — comment "Throttle other users to once every 60 seconds" but the key is per-URL and global, not per-user; staff never set the key at all.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, the Redis throttle key is `"retrieved:#{@embed_url}"`, which is intentionally URL-scoped and therefore global across callers. The comment “Throttle other users to once every 60 seconds” can reasonably be interpreted as “throttle non-staff retrieval attempts for this embed URL” rather than “per-user throttling,” so this is not a clear defect. Also, staff bypassing the throttle (`return false if @opts[:no_throttle]`) means they don’t set the key, but `perform_retrieve` immediately bails out if `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`, so a successful staff retrieval prevents subsequent fetches anyway. This finding is more of a design preference/documentation interpretation than a verifiable problem introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:131 — comment frames raw_html as merely "skip the rendering pipeline"; it is a whole-sanitization bypass on third-party HTML.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `cook_method` enum and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses the normal cooking pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook`) and its sanitization/markup processing. The new feed/import path (`TopicEmbed.import` called from `Jobs::PollFeed`) sets `cook_method: :raw_html` and later renders via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `embed/best.html.erb`, meaning third-party HTML from RSS (`i.content`) can be rendered as-is. This is a verifiable sanitization bypass/XSS risk; the comment understates the security impact by calling it merely “skip the rendering pipeline.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/locales/server.en.yml:37 — `embed.permalink` referenced nowhere, and the same commit deleted the only Permalink-producing code. Added already dead.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `embed.permalink: "Permalink"` in `config/locales/server.en.yml`, but there is no reference to `t('embed.permalink')` (or similar) anywhere in the added embed views/controllers/models shown. adjudication_records.issue_text: config/locales/server.en.yml:768 — `embeddable_host` documented as inbound-only, but it is also the sole allowlist for outbound server-side fetches; enabling embedding silently authorizes `open()` against that host.

adjudication.rationale: The diff documents `embeddable_host` in `config/locales/server.en.yml` only as “Host that can embed the comments from this Discourse forum” (i.e., an inbound embedding setting). However, the new server-side retrieval path uses the same setting as the only host allowlist for outbound fetching: `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` allows retrieval when `URI(@embed_url).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, and then `fetch_http` calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which executes `open(url).read`. Thus, turning on embedding by setting `embeddable_host` also implicitly enables server-side HTTP GETs (via `open`) to that host for arbitrary `embed_url` paths, which is not reflected by the setting’s documentation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/locales/server.en.yml:769,771 — `feed_polling_enabled` omits that it makes every embed cache-miss run a full feed poll inline; `embed_by_username` at its default `''` makes the entire embed feature no-op with no error surfaced.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` applies to the loading branch too, while loading.html.erb:9 self-reloads every 30s, so at least one reload in two is answered from cache with the same loading page.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, the call to `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is unconditional and occurs after the `if/else` that either builds `@topic_view` or `render 'loading'`. In Rails, `render` does not automatically return from the action, so the expires/cache headers will also be set on the loading response. Since `loading.html.erb` triggers `document.location.reload()` every 30 seconds, a client/proxy honoring the 1-minute caching could serve the cached loading page on subsequent reloads (e.g., every other reload), delaying the transition to the real content even after the topic has been retrieved.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:1-9 — the `posts.blank?` branch renders a single naked button: no body, no footer, no copy.

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/embed/best.html.erb, when @topic_view.posts is not present, the template still renders a header containing a “Begin the Discussion” link and the logo, and then simply skips the posts/footer section due to the later `if @topic_view.posts.present?` block. That behavior is intentional/consistent with the condition and not a clear correctness/bug defect—it's primarily a UX/design preference rather than a verifiable problem introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:8-11 — resize sent only from `window.onload`; never recomputed after images load or on resize, and the iframe has no initial height.

adjudication.rationale: The embed layout posts a single `{type:'discourse-resize', height: ...}` message only inside `window.onload` (app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:7-14). There is no handler for `window.onresize` (or any later reflow/content changes), so if the iframe’s width changes after load (responsive container, orientation change, etc.), the embedded page can reflow to a different height but the parent iframe height will not be updated, potentially clipping content (since `scrolling = "no"` in app/assets/javascripts/embed.js). It’s also true the iframe element is created without an explicit initial height (embed.js sets width but not height), so it will rely on the browser default until the first postMessage arrives. The “after images load” part is less accurate because `window.onload` typically fires after images in the iframe have loaded, but the lack of recomputation on later resize/reflow is a real defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:5,12 — no null check on `getElementById('discourse-comments')`; absent container throws and the message listener is never registered.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, `comments` is set via `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then immediately used as `comments.appendChild(iframe);` with no guard. If the host page does not include an element with id `discourse-comments`, `comments` will be `null` and this will throw a runtime error, aborting the IIFE before `window.addEventListener('message', ...)` is registered. This is a real, directly verifiable defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7 — `discourseUrl + "embed/best?…"` assumes a trailing slash with no guard, and neither global is defined or documented anywhere in the repo.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `embed.js` that explicitly declares `discourseUrl` and `discourseEmbedUrl` as expected globals (`/* global ... */`), which strongly suggests they are intended to be provided by the embedding host page rather than defined inside this repo. The diff also does not show `embed.js` being automatically included anywhere in the Discourse app, so it’s not verifiable from the diff that this will run without those globals and crash. Likewise, whether a trailing slash is required depends on how `discourseUrl` is meant to be set; the diff does not establish that it’s ever set without a trailing slash. Therefore the finding is not a clearly verifiable defect from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33 — the `url = i.id` fallback fires exactly when link isn't http(s), but import then rejects non-http(s) URLs; fallback and validation are at cross purposes and the item is dropped with no log.

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, the code sets `url = i.link` then falls back to `url = i.id` when `link` is blank or not `http(s)` (`url !~ /^https?\:\/\//`). It then calls `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, ...)`. But `TopicEmbed.import` immediately returns unless `url` matches the same `http(s)` regex (`return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`). Therefore, for feed items whose `link` is missing/non-http(s) and whose `id` is also non-http(s) (common in Atom feeds where `id` can be `tag:`/URN), the item will be silently skipped (no logging/handling in `poll_feed`). This is a real, verifiable behavior present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — Referer-only access control with no fallback; browsers legitimately strip Referer (Referrer-Policy, https→http downgrade), permanently 403ing those embeds.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is granted only if `URI(request.referer || '').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`; when the Referer header is legitimately absent/stripped (e.g., Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, some privacy settings, or certain scheme transitions), `request.referer` is nil so `URI('').host` is nil and the controller raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` (403/404-style failure). There is no alternate validation mechanism (e.g., signed token, explicit allowed origin param), so such embeds will be blocked. This behavior is also codified by the spec that expects an error when there is no referer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 + lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 — no normalization anywhere: `EXAMPLE.com` vs `example.com`, `www.` vs apex, or an admin pasting `http://example.com` into the setting all silently brick embedding.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. Both `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` compare `URI(...).host` directly to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` using string equality (`!=`), with no normalization or validation. This will reject otherwise-equivalent hosts if the setting contains a URL with scheme/port/path (e.g. `http://example.com`), different casing (hostnames are case-insensitive), or if you expect `www.example.com` and `example.com` to be treated as equivalent. The diff shows no code that normalizes/strips these, so embedding can fail due to common configuration/input variations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:18-28 — "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" are vacuous: feed_polling_enabled defaults to false and isn't stubbed, so execute short-circuits on the first condition. Both would still pass if their guards were deleted.

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#execute, poll_feed is only called when all three conditions are true: feed_polling_enabled?, feed_polling_url.present?, and embed_by_username.present?. In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, the examples "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" stub only feed_polling_url (to nil) or embed_by_username (to nil), but do not stub feed_polling_enabled? to true. Given the default in config/site_settings.yml is feed_polling_enabled: false, execute will short-circuit on the first condition and never reach the later guards, so those specs would still pass even if the feed_polling_url/embed_by_username checks were removed. This makes the two tests effectively vacuous and not actually verifying the intended behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:8-11 — "is 404 without an embed_url" never reaches params.require (the before_filter raises first on the unstubbed blank host); it duplicates the ":13" test and the ParameterMissing path is untested.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `EmbedController`, `before_filter :ensure_embeddable` runs before `best`, and `ensure_embeddable` raises if `SiteSetting.embeddable_host.blank?` or if referer host mismatches. In the spec case `it "is 404 without an embed_url" do; get :best; ... end`, no `embeddable_host` is stubbed and no referer is set, so the request will fail in the before_filter (most likely on blank `embeddable_host`, given the new default '' in `site_settings.yml`) and will not reach `params.require(:embed_url)`. That means the example passes for the wrong reason and does not exercise the `ParameterMissing` path; it effectively overlaps with the later "missing host" coverage rather than testing missing `embed_url`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:22-26 — no mismatched-referer, https-vs-http, or `www.` case; the core of ensure_embeddable is untested.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` enforces `URI(request.referer || '').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (and rescues `URI::InvalidURIError`). The added spec (`spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`) covers: missing `embed_url`, missing `embeddable_host`, no referer, and the success case where referer equals the embed_url. It does not include any test where the referer is present but the host mismatches `embeddable_host`, nor any edge cases like `www.` vs non-`www` or scheme differences; it also doesn’t exercise the invalid-URI rescue path. So the finding about missing test coverage for the key host-matching behavior is verifiably true in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Two lens agents disagreed on whether `<%- end if %>` is a hard `SyntaxError` or merely misordered output — that's stdlib ERB vs Rails 4's Erubis. Both compiled it and both confirm it's defective; only the failure mode differs.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, the header block opens with `<%- if @topic_view.posts.present? %>` and later closes with `<%- end if %>`. The generated Ruby code would contain `end if`, which is not valid Ruby syntax (Ruby allows modifier `if` on expressions, but `end if` is a SyntaxError). This will cause the template to fail compilation/rendering under ERB/Erubis.
